Title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Swagger UI HTML Generation
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis:
The function `get_swagger_ui_html` in `fastapi/openapi/docs.py` compiles an HTML document containing interactive documentation powered by Swagger UI. It uses Python f-strings to format several variables directly into HTML context and `<script>` blocks without performing any sanitization or context-aware HTML/JavaScript escaping.

#### 1. JavaScript String Injection via `openapi_url` and `oauth2_redirect_url`:
The `openapi_url` parameter is directly formatted inside single-quotes within a `<script>` tag:
```javascript
const ui = SwaggerUIBundle({
    url: '{openapi_url}',
```
If an attacker controls or influences `openapi_url` (e.g., via the application's ASGI `root_path` which is often populated from dynamic HTTP proxy headers, or in custom routes using query parameters), they can easily break out of the JavaScript string literal and execute arbitrary JS code.

#### 2. HTML Script Tag Breakout in JSON-serialized values:
The function serializes `swagger_ui_parameters` and `init_oauth` with `json.dumps` and embeds them directly inside the same `<script>` block. While `json.dumps` prevents standard JavaScript string breakouts by escaping quotes, it does **not** escape HTML closing tags (such as `</script>`). Because HTML parsing occurs before JavaScript execution, if an attacker controls a key or value in these objects and sets it to `</script><script>alert(1)</script>`, the browser HTML parser closes the current script block and opens a new one, leading to stored/reflected XSS.

#### 3. HTML Injection / XSS via `title`, `swagger_js_url`, `swagger_css_url`, and `swagger_favicon_url`:
All of these attributes are formatted directly into the HTML body/head. If any of these are dynamically derived from external configuration, a database, or user headers, an attacker can perform arbitrary HTML/CSS injection or execute scripts.

### Source:
Untrusted parameters passed to `get_swagger_ui_html` (e.g. `openapi_url` dynamically constructed via ASGI `root_path` derived from request headers, or developer-configured dynamic variables).

### Sanitization/Validation:
None. No HTML-escaping or JS-escaping is performed.

### Sink:
The unescaped HTML string is returned within a Starlette `HTMLResponse` block at line 158:
```python
return HTMLResponse(html)
```

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
#### Scenario A (Single Quote JS breakout):
If `openapi_url` is configured or manipulated to be:
`'; alert(document.domain); //`

The rendered JavaScript outputs:
```javascript
const ui = SwaggerUIBundle({
    url: ''; alert(document.domain); //',
```
Resulting in the execution of `alert(document.domain)`.

#### Scenario B (Script Tag breakout):
If `init_oauth` is configured to contain a parameter:
`{"client_id": "</script><script>alert(1)</script>"}`

The rendered HTML outputs:
```html
<script>
...
ui.initOAuth({"client_id": "</script><script>alert(1)</script>"})
</script>
```
The browser parses `</script>`, closes the first block, and immediately executes `alert(1)` in the second block.

Title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in ReDoc HTML Generation
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis:
The function `get_redoc_html` in `fastapi/openapi/docs.py` compiles an HTML document containing interactive documentation powered by ReDoc. Similar to `get_swagger_ui_html`, it uses Python f-strings to format several variables directly into HTML context without any sanitization or context-aware escaping.

#### 1. HTML Attribute Injection via `openapi_url`:
The `openapi_url` parameter is directly formatted inside double quotes within the `<redoc>` custom HTML element:
```html
<redoc spec-url="{openapi_url}"></redoc>
```
If an attacker controls or influences `openapi_url` (e.g., via the application's ASGI `root_path` derived from request headers or dynamic routing), they can break out of the HTML attribute by injecting a double quote (`"`) and insert arbitrary event handlers (like `onload` or `onmouseover`) or separate tags.

#### 2. HTML Injection / XSS via `title`, `redoc_js_url`, and `redoc_favicon_url`:
The variables `title`, `redoc_js_url`, and `redoc_favicon_url` are formatted directly into the HTML body/head. If any of these are dynamically derived from external inputs, an attacker can perform arbitrary HTML injection, script injection, or CSS injection.

### Source:
Untrusted parameters passed to `get_redoc_html` (e.g. `openapi_url` dynamically constructed via ASGI `root_path` derived from request headers, or developer-configured dynamic variables).

### Sanitization/Validation:
None. No HTML-escaping is performed.

### Sink:
The unescaped HTML string is returned within a Starlette `HTMLResponse` block at line 253:
```python
return HTMLResponse(html)
```

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
If `openapi_url` is manipulated to be:
`" autofocus onfocus="alert(document.cookie)`

The rendered HTML outputs:
```html
<redoc spec-url="" autofocus onfocus="alert(document.cookie)"></redoc>
```
When parsed by the browser, the event handler will immediately execute, leading to stored/reflected XSS.
Snippet:
html = f"""

    <html>
    <head>
    <title>{title}</title>
    <!-- needed for adaptive design -->
    <meta charset="utf-8"/>
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    """
    if with_google_fonts:
        html += """
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Montserrat:300,400,700|Roboto:300,400,700" rel="stylesheet">
    """
    html += f"""
